To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the surface mobility of cations on the oxide surface is dependent on the nature and geometry of the surface, and on the size of the cation and the elementary cell of oxide.
the structure of the conducting channels is primarily dependent on the size of the cation, whereas energy barriers depend on the nature of the mobile cations and the structure of the elementary cell.
the surface mobility of cations depends primarily on the nature of the cation and on the structure of the surface of the oxide, and is only weakly dependent on the nature and structure of the oxide.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new methods of modelling the surface transport of protons and cations in the presence of water molecules and the application of these models to study of the surface properties of oxide materials.
the study of surface mobility of single-charged cationic impurity on the surface of oxide crystals with rutile structure.

the development of new methods of modelling of the surface processes in the systems with complex structure, and with the analysis of the influence of structural features of the surface on the mobility of the surface cations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the surface mobility of cations on the surfaces of oxides with rutile-type structure depends on both the nature of the cation and the nature of the oxide.

the transport of single-charged cation over the surface of rutiles depends on the size of the cation, the structure and geometry as well as the size of the unit cell of the oxide, and the nature of the cations.
, the transport of single-charged cation over the surface of rutiles depends on the size and radius of the mobile cations, as well as the geometry of the surface and the structure of the oxide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the energy barriers of the surface mobility for protons and other monovalent cations are comparable, and that the surface diffusion of protons is not hindered by their small size.
the energy barriers are the lowest for the smallest ions, and the highest for the largest ones.
the surface mobility of single-charged cation on the surface of oxide is determined by the nature of mobile ion, the geometry of the conducting channel and the structure of the oxide lattice.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the surface mobility of cations in the surface layers of the oxides of group 4 elements having rutile structure is determined not only by the radius of the mobile ions but also by the size of the unit cell of the oxides.

the mobility of cations on the surfaces of oxides with rutile structure is determined by the size of the cation and the geometry of the conducting channel, which is primarily determined by the size and geometry of the elementary cell.
, for the same size of the elementary unit cell, the energy of the activation barrier is lower for the transport of protons than for the transport of other cations.
